questions.q: What does terraform.tfstate primarily record that your .tf configuration files do not?
options: The provider's API credentials
The real resource IDs the cloud provider assigned when resources were created
A copy of the Terraform CLI binary
The order lessons appear in this course
questions.explain: Your configuration describes desired resources and attributes, but never the real IDs a provider assigns at creation time. State is where Terraform records that mapping.

questions.q: What is 'drift' in the context of Terraform state?
options: A bug in the Terraform CLI itself
When real infrastructure no longer matches what state and configuration say should exist
The time delay between plan and apply
A type of remote backend
questions.explain: Drift happens when something changes a resource outside of Terraform -- for example editing it by hand in a console -- so reality no longer matches the recorded state.

questions.q: During terraform plan, what does the 'refresh' step do?
options: Deletes the local .tf files
Reads the real provider API and compares it against state before reporting any differences
Downloads a new version of Terraform
Rewrites your configuration automatically
questions.explain: Refreshing means Terraform queries the real provider API for current attributes, then compares that against state and your configuration to detect drift.

questions.q: If terraform.tfstate is deleted, what is the most accurate description of what happens?
options: Nothing changes -- Terraform rebuilds it automatically from the .tf files
Terraform no longer knows the resources it created exist, and may try to recreate them on the next apply
The real infrastructure in Azure or AWS is immediately deleted
Terraform refuses to run any command ever again
questions.explain: Losing state doesn't delete real infrastructure, but it does mean Terraform has no record of what it already built -- running apply again risks creating duplicates.

questions.q: In the sample state entry for azurerm_resource_group.northbridge, what does the 'id' attribute represent?
options: A random value Terraform generates for internal bookkeeping only
The full Azure resource ID returned by Azure when the resource group was actually created
The local name used inside the .tf configuration file
The Terraform version that created the resource
questions.explain: The id attribute is the real resource ID Azure assigned at creation time -- something that never existed in the .tf configuration until Terraform recorded it in state.
